name: Content Coverage
description: Measures how well the summary captures the key points and findings of the original research paper, including important concepts, results, and conclusions.
scale: 0-100% (0% means no key points covered, 100% means all key points covered)

name: Clarity and Coherence
description: Evaluates the clarity and logical flow of the summary, assessing how easily the reader can understand the main ideas presented.
scale: 0-10 (0 means very unclear and incoherent, 10 means very clear and coherent)

name: Conciseness
description: Assesses the brevity of the summary while ensuring that it remains informative. A good summary should be succinct without losing essential information.
scale: 0-10 (0 means overly verbose, 10 means perfectly concise)

name: Relevance
description: Measures the relevance of the summary to the original paper, including whether it stays on topic and reflects the main themes of the research.
scale: 0-10 (0 means not relevant at all, 10 means highly relevant)

name: Technical Accuracy
description: Evaluates the accuracy of the scientific and technical information presented in the summary, including the correct use of terminology and the validity of claims made.
scale: 0-10 (0 means highly inaccurate, 10 means fully accurate)
